sources: https://17jewels.info/movements/e/eta/eta-2824-2/ (20-tooth steel escape wheel, direct centre seconds, no true centre wheel)
notes: No true centre wheel: the great wheel sits off centre at 5 o'clock and its period is not known, so it is left out; the minute hand's cannon pinion turns once an hour. 38 h power reserve. Tooth counts of the third and fourth wheels and the barrel were not found. The 2836-2 and 2834-2 add day and date to the same base. The clone on Peter's bench is recorded as '2824-2'.

sources: https://atelierhorlogerie.com/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/the-valjoux-7750-chronograph-doc.pdf (Odets: off-centre centre wheel, indirect motion work, chronograph driven from the fourth wheel)
notes: Lift angle: 49° in the AWCI table, 50° is also widely used. The centre wheel is off centre and the motion work is driven through an intermediate wheel, so its period is left out. Escape wheel tooth count not found. Some early 7750s ran at 21,600 vph; this entry is the 28,800 version. 'Daytona 4130' clones built on a 7750 base use this train plus extra wheels to move the small seconds to 6.

notes: The only calibre here with a published train: escape 15 teeth on a 10-leaf pinion, fourth 120/8, third 60/10, centre 80 teeth (centre pinion and barrel not found, so the barrel is left out). The counts fit 21,600 vph, the -2 versions. The -1 versions run at 18,000 vph with a train not found; they are not in this entry. 56 h power reserve.
